source_title: Morning Digest: In Delhi, BJP booth agents file deletion forms against Muslim voters living at their addresses; Supreme Court says order on fireworks breached, and more
source_excerpt: In Delhi, BJP booth agents file deletion forms against Muslim voters living at their addresses BJP BLAs submit nearly 68% of Form 7s seeking deletions as ‘objector’ in Mustafabad, all against Muslim electors, citing ‘absent/permanently shifted’ or ‘death’. The Mustafabad constituency has seen the highest number of Form 7 applications, with 843 objections since August 31. Of the 597 forms filed by third parties, 96% name BLAs from the BJP as ‘objectors’; 572 Form 7s filed by these BLAs are against Muslim electors across 24 parts of the constituency. In Delhi, BJP booth agents file deletion forms against Muslim voters living at their addresses storyline 1 Our orders breached ‘left and right’, Deepavali was a festival of lights before gunpowder, Supreme Court says in firecrackers case The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said its orders, year after year, to curb and even ban firecrackers during Deepavali had been violated “left and right”. A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale said the right to religious freedom was also subject to public health and the protection of fundamental rights. Our orders breached ‘left and right’, Deepavali was a festival of lights before gunpowder, Supreme Court says in firecrackers case storyline 1 Supreme Court calls for financial institutions to compensate digital arrest victims The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) called on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to mandate financial institutions to fully indemnify digital arrest victims if the crime happened due to a lack of institutional diligence. Expressing “frustration” at digital arrest scamsters siphoning off crores from the national economy annually, the court also questioned how educated people remained gullible enough to believe they can be detained over mobile phone calls.
